problem:
$$
∃\,\,{m}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{I}\end{aligned}}\in Z,\,{n}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{II}\end{aligned}}\,|\,{m}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{III}\end{aligned}}
$$

Which occurrences of the variables in the expression above are free?
worked_solution:
Let's examine our expression and mark the occurrences of the variables as bound $(\text{b})$ or free $(\text{f}).$

- Occurrence I of the variable $m$ is *bound* since it's placed right next to the quantifier $∃:$

$$
∃\,\,{m}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in Z,\,n\,|\,m
$$

- Occurrence II of the variable $n$ is *free* since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $n.$

- Occurrence III of the variable $m$ is *bound* since it lies within the scope of the quantifier $∃m$ that uses $m:$

$$
∃\,\,m\in Z,\,\,\overset{\text{scope of }∃m}{\overset{⏞}{n\,|\,{m}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}}}
$$

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows:

$$
∃\,\,{m}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in Z,\,{n}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{f}\end{aligned}}\,|\,{m}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}
$$

Therefore, the free occurrence is "II only."
